newsitem.title: UK: Halifax to indicate conversion price in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Halifax to indicate conversion price in Jan.

text.p: Britain's Halifax Building Society said on Thursday it would send its members in January 1997, the transfer document for its planned stock exchange flotation and conversion to bank status.
The building society said in a statement this would contain "an indication of the likely price range of Halifax shares based on prevailing market conditions at the date of the document".
It also confirmed that if members vote in favour of conversion and all the regulatory procedures are satisfied, its shares will be listed on the London Stock Exchange in June,1997.

The Halifax said the document will inform members of the number of shares they could be entitled to receive. It will be accompanied by voting forms and members -- the society's savers and borrowers -- will be urged to vote "as quickly as possible". The society needs at least 50 percent of all investing members to vote in favour to secure approval for its conversion.

A special general meeting to consider conversion will be held in February in Sheffield. Halifax also said it will, if it gets regulatory approval, set up a share dealing service for what will be "the largest single extension of private share ownership ever witnessed in the UK".

Those of the around nine million investors on the Halifax share register who decide to cash in their windfalls, will be offered a postal service, free-of-charge. Halifax said it had decided to convert by transferring its business to an existing subsidiary company, rather than to a specially-formed company.
